question: Which of the following cell organelles have enough surface area for ATP-generating chemical reactions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mitochondria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because they generate ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) through cellular respiration.

 

• The inner membrane of the mitochondrion is folded into finger-like projections called cristae, which greatly increase the surface area available for the enzymes and electron-transport-chain proteins that carry out ATP-generating reactions.

 

• Mitochondria have their own circular DNA and ribosomes and can therefore make some of their own proteins; they are believed to have originated from free-living bacteria (endosymbiotic theory).

 

Additional Information

 

• Lysosomes, called the 'suicide bags' of the cell, contain digestive enzymes and break down waste material and worn-out cell parts.

 

• Vacuoles are fluid-filled sacs used for storage; plant cells have one large central vacuole that maintains turgidity.

 

• The cell wall, found in plant cells, is a rigid outer covering made of cellulose that gives shape and protection, but plays no role in ATP generation.

 

NOTE

 

• Lysosomes (Option B): Involved in digestion of cell debris, not energy production.

 

• Vacuoles (Option C): Mainly for storage of water, ions and waste products.

 

• Cell wall (Option D): A structural, protective covering with no role in respiration.

question: Generally which of the following trophic levels have the least number of organisms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tertiary consumers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a food chain, energy and numbers of organisms decrease at each successive trophic level, following the 10% law of energy transfer proposed by Lindeman.

 

• This creates an ecological pyramid of numbers that is generally upright: Producers > Primary consumers > Secondary consumers > Tertiary consumers.

 

• Tertiary consumers (top carnivores, e.g. lions, eagles) sit at the apex of the food chain and therefore have the least number of organisms, since only about 10% of energy is passed on from one level to the next.

 

Additional Information

 

• Producers (green plants) are the most numerous as they trap solar energy directly through photosynthesis and form the base of the pyramid.

 

• Primary consumers (herbivores) feed directly on producers; secondary consumers (small carnivores) feed on primary consumers.

 

NOTE

 

• Secondary consumers (Option A) and Primary consumers (Option D) occupy middle trophic levels with intermediate numbers.

 

• Producers (Option C) are the most abundant, forming the widest base of the ecological pyramid.

question: Which of the following has straight-chain hydrocarbons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Butane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Butane (n-Butane, C₄H₁₀) is a straight-chain (unbranched) alkane — its four carbon atoms are joined in a single continuous chain: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃.

 

• A hydrocarbon is called straight-chain when its carbon skeleton has no side branches; it is called branched-chain when a carbon atom is attached to more than two other carbon atoms.

 

• 3-Methylpentane, Isobutane and 2-Methylpropane are all branched-chain hydrocarbons — note that Isobutane and 2-Methylpropane are actually the same compound (methylpropane) named differently.

 

Additional Information

 

• Straight-chain and branched-chain compounds having the same molecular formula are called chain isomers, e.g. n-butane and isobutane (both C₄H₁₀).

 

• The general formula of alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, regardless of whether the chain is straight or branched.

 

NOTE

 

• 3-Methylpentane (Option B): A branched hexane isomer with a methyl group on the third carbon.

 

• Isobutane (Option C) and 2-Methylpropane (Option D): Both refer to the same branched isomer of butane.

question: A body of mass 'm' kg is kept at a height of 'h' m from the surface of the Earth. What will be the potential energy possessed by this body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is mgh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gravitational potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position relative to the Earth's surface.

 

• It is given by the formula P.E. = mgh, where m is the mass of the body, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is the height above the reference surface.

 

• The SI unit of potential energy is the joule (J), same as all forms of energy.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kinetic energy, the energy of motion, is given by K.E. = ½mv².

 

• By the law of conservation of energy, as a body falls, its potential energy converts into kinetic energy, and the total mechanical energy remains constant (ignoring air resistance).

 

NOTE

 

• The other options do not represent the dimensionally correct or standard formula for gravitational potential energy.

question: How much work (W) is done in moving a charge (Q) of 5 C across two points that have a potential difference of 15 V?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 75 J.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Potential difference (V) between two points is defined as the work done (W) per unit charge (Q) in moving a charge between them: V = W/Q, so W = QV.

 

• Here, Q = 5 C and V = 15 V, so W = 5 × 15 = 75 joules.

 

• The SI unit of potential difference is the volt (V), where 1 volt = 1 joule/coulomb.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electric current (I) is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q/t, measured in amperes.

 

• Electric power is given by P = VI = I²R = V²/R, measured in watts.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is dividing instead of multiplying (giving 15/5 = 3 J, Option B) — remember W = QV, not V/Q.

question: Which of the following statements is true about HIV transmission?
option_1: HIV can be transmitted through mosquito bites.
option_2: HIV can be transmitted through casual contact.
option_3: HIV can be transmitted through aerosols.
option_4: HIV can be transmitted through sexual acts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is HIV can be transmitted through sexual acts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), the causative agent of AIDS, is primarily transmitted through unprotected sexual contact with an infected person, as the virus is present in semen and vaginal fluids.

 

• Other confirmed modes of transmission include: transfusion of infected blood, sharing of infected/contaminated needles and syringes (common among IV drug users), and from an infected mother to her child during pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding (vertical transmission).

 

• HIV attacks and destroys helper T-lymphocytes (CD4 cells) of the immune system, severely weakening the body's ability to fight infections.

 

Additional Information

 

• HIV cannot spread through casual contact such as shaking hands, hugging, sharing food/utensils, or through the air (aerosols/coughing/sneezing), or through insect/mosquito bites, because the virus does not survive or replicate in these vectors.

 

• AIDS (Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome) was first identified in 1981; the ELISA test and Western blot test are used to diagnose HIV infection.

 

NOTE

 

• Mosquito bites (Option A): Unlike malaria parasites, HIV cannot survive or multiply inside a mosquito, so it is not transmitted this way.

 

• Casual contact (Option B) and Aerosols (Option C): Both are common myths; HIV does not spread through the air or routine social contact.

question: How is intercropping beneficial over single crop farming?
option_1: Utilises nutrients efficiently and prevents spread of diseases
solution_text:
The correct answer is Utilises nutrients efficiently and prevents spread of diseases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Intercropping is the practice of growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite row pattern (e.g. one row of a legume between two rows of a cereal).

 

• Different crops have different nutrient requirements and root depths, so growing them together allows more efficient use of soil nutrients, water and sunlight, since the crops do not compete for exactly the same resources.

 

• Since the crops are of different species, a disease or pest that attacks one crop is less likely to spread to the other crop growing alongside it, unlike in single-crop (monoculture) farming where an outbreak can devastate the entire field.

 

Additional Information

 

• Growing leguminous crops (e.g. soybean, gram) with cereals also helps in natural nitrogen fixation in the soil through *Rhizobium* bacteria present in their root nodules.

 

• Crop rotation, in contrast, is growing different crops on the same land in a sequence over different seasons, which helps restore soil fertility and break pest cycles.

 

NOTE

 

• Reduces labour cost (Option B): Intercropping generally needs more careful management, not necessarily less labour.

 

• Increases irrigation needs (Option C) and Requires less land (Option D): Neither is the primary advantage of intercropping; the key benefit is efficient resource use and disease control.

question: Why can tiny molecules like oxygen easily pass through the cell membrane, but not the big ones like starch or proteins?
option_1: Small molecules have special energy to push through.
option_2: Big molecules have to break down for entry.
option_3: The cell membrane is permeable to selective substances.
option_4: The cell membrane is completely solid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The cell membrane is permeable to selective substances.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cell (plasma) membrane is described as selectively (semi-) permeable, meaning it allows only certain substances — usually small molecules like oxygen, carbon dioxide and water — to pass through freely, while blocking or regulating the passage of larger molecules like starch and proteins.

 

• This selective permeability is due to the membrane's structure, described by the fluid mosaic model, which consists of a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins that act as channels/carriers for specific substances.

 

• Small, non-polar molecules like O₂ and CO₂ can diffuse directly across the lipid bilayer, whereas large or polar molecules need specific transport proteins or must first be broken down (digested) into smaller units before they can cross.

 

Additional Information

 

• Movement of substances across the membrane occurs via diffusion (high to low concentration, no energy needed), osmosis (movement of water), and active transport (needs ATP energy, moves against concentration gradient).

 

• The plasma membrane is composed mainly of lipids and proteins, giving it flexibility as well as selective control over what enters and leaves the cell.

 

NOTE

 

• Small molecules have special energy (Option A): Incorrect; O₂ moves by simple diffusion, requiring no special energy.

 

• Big molecules have to break down (Option B): Partially true for digestion but does not explain the membrane's fundamental property.

 

• Completely solid (Option D): Incorrect; the membrane is fluid and flexible, not rigid or solid.

question: The weight of a body on the moon is less than on Earth because:
option_2: Mass of the body decreases on the moon
option_3: Mass of the moon is equal to Earth's mass
option_4: Gravitational acceleration on the moon is smaller
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gravitational acceleration on the moon is smaller.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Weight (W = mg) depends on both the mass of the body and the local acceleration due to gravity (g).

 

• The Moon's gravitational acceleration is about 1.63 m/s², roughly one-sixth of the Earth's value (9.8 m/s²), because the Moon has a much smaller mass than the Earth (g = GM/R²).

 

• Since g is smaller on the Moon, the weight of the same body becomes less there, even though its mass stays exactly the same everywhere in the universe.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mass is a scalar quantity, measured in kilograms, and does not change with location; weight is a vector force, measured in newtons, and varies with the value of g.

 

• The Moon has no atmosphere because its weak gravity cannot hold gas molecules — but this fact explains the absence of air/weather on the Moon, not directly why weight is less.

 

NOTE

 

• No atmosphere (Option A): A true fact about the Moon, but not the reason weight decreases.

 

• Mass decreases (Option B): Incorrect — mass is constant regardless of location.

 

• Moon's mass equal to Earth's (Option C): Factually false; the Moon's mass is only about 1/81st of Earth's mass.

question: Which of the following human diseases can be transmitted during sexual act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• AIDS, caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), is a sexually transmitted disease (STD); it can also spread through infected blood, contaminated needles, and from mother to child.

 

• Other common sexually transmitted infections (STIs) include gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydia and genital warts.

 

• STIs are diseases spread mainly through sexual contact, unlike genetic, nutritional or lifestyle disorders.

 

Additional Information

 

• Protein Energy Malnutrition (PEM) is a nutritional deficiency disorder caused by inadequate intake of proteins and calories, seen in conditions like kwashiorkor and marasmus.

 

• Diabetes is a metabolic disorder related to insulin deficiency or resistance, not an infectious disease.

 

• Cancer is an uncontrolled cell-division disorder; while some cancers (e.g. cervical cancer) are linked to STIs like HPV, cancer itself is not classified as a sexually transmitted disease.

 

NOTE

 

• Protein Energy Malnutrition (Option A): A nutritional deficiency disorder, not infectious.

 

• Diabetes (Option B): A metabolic/hormonal disorder related to insulin.

 

• Cancer (Option D): A cellular disorder, not transmitted through sexual contact.

question: Which of the following will show diffusion fastest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gas in gas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diffusion is the spontaneous movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration due to their kinetic energy.

 

• The rate of diffusion depends on the spacing between particles and their kinetic energy: gases have particles that are very far apart and move fastest, so diffusion is quickest in a gas-in-gas system.

 

• The general order of diffusion rate is: Gases > Liquids > Solids, since intermolecular spaces decrease and intermolecular forces increase in that order.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diffusion in solids is extremely slow because particles are tightly packed and can only vibrate about fixed positions.

 

• Diffusion increases with an increase in temperature, since particles gain more kinetic energy and move faster.

 

NOTE

 

• Solid in liquid (Option A) and Liquid in gas (Option B): Intermediate rates, faster than solid-solid but slower than gas-gas.

 

• Solid in solid (Option C): The slowest, as particles in solids have minimal free movement.

question: Which of the following methods involves coating steel and iron with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Galvanisation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Galvanisation is the process of coating iron or steel with a thin protective layer of zinc to prevent rusting (corrosion).

 

• Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes (oxidises) preferentially, protecting the underlying iron even if the zinc coating gets scratched — this is called sacrificial protection.

 

• Galvanised iron sheets are commonly used for roofing, pipes, buckets, and wire fencing due to their rust resistance.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electroplating is a broader technique of depositing any metal (e.g. chromium, gold, nickel) onto another surface using electrolysis, mainly for decorative or protective purposes — galvanisation with zinc via dipping (hot-dip galvanising) is a related but distinct process.

 

• Cathodic protection is a technique to prevent corrosion by making the metal to be protected the cathode of an electrochemical cell, often using a sacrificial anode (like magnesium or zinc) connected to it.

 

• Passivation involves treating a metal surface (e.g. with nitric acid) to make it less reactive and form a protective oxide layer.

 

NOTE

 

• Cathodic protection (Option A): Uses an external sacrificial metal connected electrically, not a coating.

 

• Electroplating (Option B): A general term for depositing metal via electric current, not specific to zinc-iron rust prevention.

 

• Passivation (Option C): Involves chemical surface treatment, not a zinc coating.

question: Which of the following plants reproduces asexually by budding along the margins of a leaf?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bryophyllum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bryophyllum (also called the 'miracle leaf' or 'air plant') reproduces asexually through vegetative propagation — tiny buds (adventitious buds) develop along the notches/margins of its leaves.

 

• When these leaves fall onto soil, the buds grow into new, independent plantlets, allowing rapid multiplication without seeds.

 

• This is a form of vegetative propagation, a type of asexual reproduction seen widely in plants.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hydra, a simple animal, reproduces asexually by budding too, but from its body wall, not a leaf margin — this is an animal example, not a plant one.

 

• Mango is propagated commercially via grafting, a form of artificial vegetative propagation, and reproduces sexually through seeds in nature.

 

• Spirogyra, a green alga, reproduces asexually by fragmentation and sexually by conjugation.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydra (Option A): Reproduces by budding, but is an animal, not a plant with leaves.

 

• Mango (Option C): Propagated by grafting/seeds, not leaf-margin budding.

 

• Spirogyra (Option D): Reproduces by fragmentation, an algal (not leaf-based) mechanism.

question: Which of the following observations best supports that liquids have a definite volume but no fixed shape?
option_1: Air expands to fill the entire container
option_2: A solid iron block retains its shape in any container
option_3: Water takes the shape of its container but retains its volume
option_4: A sponge changes its shape when squeezed
solution_text:
The correct answer is Water takes the shape of its container but retains its volume.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Liquids have a definite (fixed) volume but no fixed shape — they take the shape of whatever container they are poured into, while the total amount (volume) of the liquid remains unchanged.

 

• Water is a classic example: pour the same 500 mL of water into a round flask or a tall cylinder, and it takes each container's shape, but the volume stays 500 mL in both cases.

 

• This property arises because liquid particles are closely packed but not rigidly fixed, allowing them to flow and rearrange while still remaining close together overall.

 

Additional Information

 

• Solids have both a fixed shape and fixed volume, since their particles are tightly packed in a fixed arrangement with strong intermolecular forces.

 

• Gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume — they expand to completely fill any container, as their particles have large gaps and move freely.

 

NOTE

 

• Air expanding (Option A): Illustrates a property of gases (no fixed shape or volume), not liquids.

 

• Solid iron block (Option B): Illustrates the property of solids (fixed shape and volume).

 

• Sponge changing shape (Option D): A physical/mechanical property of a porous solid, unrelated to the liquid state of matter.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of gases?
option_1: No fixed shape and no fixed volume
option_4: No fixed shape but fixed volume
solution_text:
The correct answer is No fixed shape and no fixed volume.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume — they expand to completely occupy the shape and volume of whatever container holds them.

 

• This happens because gas particles are very far apart, move randomly at high speed, and have negligible intermolecular forces between them.

 

• Gases are also highly compressible and fluid (they flow), unlike what Option B states.

 

Additional Information

 

• Solids have fixed shape and fixed volume (strong intermolecular forces, particles vibrate in fixed positions).

 

• Liquids have a fixed volume but no fixed shape (particles close together but free to move past one another).

 

• The kinetic theory of matter explains these differences based on the spacing, motion, and forces between particles in the three states.

 

NOTE

 

• Compressible but not fluid (Option B): Incorrect — gases are both compressible AND fluid (they flow easily).

 

• Fixed shape and volume (Option C): This describes solids, not gases.

 

• No fixed shape but fixed volume (Option D): This describes liquids, not gases.

question: The relation between electric energy, power and time is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Energy = Power × Time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electric power (P) is defined as the rate of doing electrical work, i.e. the energy consumed or produced per unit time: P = W/t.

 

• Rearranging this formula gives Electric Energy (W) = Power (P) × Time (t).

 

• The commercial unit of electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh), commonly known as a 'unit' of electricity, where 1 kWh = 1000 watts used for 1 hour = 3.6 × 10⁶ joules.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of power is the watt (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second.

 

• The SI unit of energy is the joule (J).

 

• Electrical power can also be expressed as P = VI = I²R = V²/R, using Ohm's law relations.

 

NOTE

 

• The other options do not represent a dimensionally or physically correct relation between energy, power and time.

question: When we hit a table lightly, the sound produced is soft because the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is amplitude of vibration is small.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The loudness of a sound depends on the amplitude of the vibration producing it — larger amplitude means a louder sound, and smaller amplitude means a softer sound.

 

• When we hit the table lightly, we impart less energy, causing the table's surface to vibrate with a small amplitude, producing a soft sound.

 

• Hitting the table hard would impart more energy, producing vibrations of larger amplitude and hence a louder sound.

 

Additional Information

 

• The pitch (shrillness) of a sound depends on its frequency — higher frequency gives a higher pitch, and this is unrelated to loudness.

 

• The quality (timbre) of sound helps distinguish between two sounds of the same loudness and pitch (e.g. a violin and a flute playing the same note).

 

• Loudness is measured in decibels (dB).

 

NOTE

 

• Frequency being low (Option B): Frequency determines pitch, not loudness — a soft hit doesn't necessarily change frequency.

 

• Speed of sound decreasing (Option C): The speed of sound depends on the medium and temperature, not on how hard the table is struck.

 

• Wavelength becoming shorter (Option D): Wavelength is related to frequency (pitch), not to loudness/softness.

question: When a gun is fired, the bullet moves forward because:
option_3: the recoil of the gun acts backward as reaction
solution_text:
The correct answer is the recoil of the gun acts backward as reaction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This phenomenon is explained by Newton's Third Law of Motion: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

• When the gun fires, the expanding gases push the bullet forward (action) with a certain force, and simultaneously the gun recoils backward (reaction) with an equal and opposite force.

 

• Because the gun has a much larger mass than the bullet, the same magnitude of force produces a much smaller backward velocity for the gun compared to the bullet's large forward velocity, in line with the law of conservation of momentum (initial momentum of the system was zero, so the forward momentum of the bullet equals the backward momentum of the gun).

 

Additional Information

 

• The recoil of a gun is a classic real-life illustration of conservation of linear momentum: m(bullet) × v(bullet) = m(gun) × v(gun, recoil).

 

• Other everyday applications of Newton's third law include the recoil of a cannon, the motion of a rocket, and a swimmer pushing water backward to move forward.

 

NOTE

 

• Gravity pushes it forward (Option A): Gravity acts vertically downward, not in the direction of the bullet's forward motion.

 

• Barrel exerts no force (Option B): Incorrect; the barrel guides and directs the expanding gas pressure onto the bullet.

 

• Air resistance acts forward (Option D): Air resistance always opposes motion, so it acts backward on a forward-moving bullet, not forward.

question: Magnification produced by a lens is related to object distance (u) and image distance (v) by the formula:
solution_text:
The correct answer is m = v / u.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Linear magnification (m) produced by a lens is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, and it is also equal to the ratio of the image distance to the object distance: m = v/u = hᵢ/hₒ.

 

• Here, v is the image distance and u is the object distance from the optical centre of the lens, measured according to the sign convention (with distances measured from the lens, and following the Cartesian sign convention in numerical problems).

 

• If |m| > 1, the image is magnified (enlarged); if |m| < 1, the image is diminished; if |m| = 1, the image is the same size as the object.

 

Additional Information

 

• The lens formula relates focal length, image distance and object distance: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

 

• A positive value of magnification indicates a virtual and erect image, while a negative value indicates a real and inverted image (for lenses, using the Cartesian sign convention).

 

NOTE

 

• The other formulas (u+v, u/v, v−u) do not correctly represent the standard definition of magnification used in optics.

question: Which among the following organic compounds is saturated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bromopropane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saturated compounds contain only single (sigma) bonds between carbon atoms, following the general formula for alkanes/alkyl derivatives (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ or their substituted forms).

 

• Bromopropane (C₃H₇Br) is a haloalkane derived from propane (a saturated alkane, CH₃–CH₂–CH₃) by replacing one hydrogen with a bromine atom — it retains only single bonds and is therefore saturated.

 

• Unsaturated compounds, by contrast, contain at least one double bond (alkenes) or triple bond (alkynes) between carbon atoms.

 

Additional Information

 

• Propyne (C₃H₄) contains a carbon-carbon triple bond (an alkyne), making it unsaturated.

 

• Propene (C₃H₆) and 2-Bromopropene both contain a carbon-carbon double bond (alkenes), making them unsaturated.

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water and alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent), a test used to distinguish them from saturated ones.

 

NOTE

 

• Propyne (Option A): Contains a triple bond — an alkyne, unsaturated.

 

• 2-Bromopropene (Option C): A brominated alkene, contains a double bond — unsaturated.

 

• Propene (Option D): A simple alkene with a double bond — unsaturated.

question: Mitochondria are special because they have their own DNA and ribosomes. What can they do on this basis?
option_1: Make some of their own proteins
option_2: Move around the cell on their own
option_3: Make food using sunlight like plants do
solution_text:
The correct answer is Make some of their own proteins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitochondria possess their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes, independent of the nuclear genome, which allows them to synthesise some of their own proteins required for cellular respiration.

 

• This unique feature supports the endosymbiotic theory, which suggests that mitochondria originated from free-living, aerobic bacteria that were engulfed by a larger primitive cell and evolved a mutually beneficial relationship over time.

 

• Because they can replicate and produce some proteins semi-independently, mitochondria are often called 'semi-autonomous organelles'.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besides mitochondria, chloroplasts (in plant cells) are the only other organelles known to have their own DNA and ribosomes, also supporting the endosymbiotic theory.

 

• Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration and ATP production, occurring via the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain on the inner membrane.

 

NOTE

 

• Move around the cell on their own (Option B): Not related to having DNA/ribosomes; this isn't a defining property based on this feature.

 

• Make food using sunlight (Option C): This is the function of chloroplasts (photosynthesis), not mitochondria.

 

• Digest materials like lysosomes (Option D): Digestion of cell debris is a lysosomal function, unrelated to mitochondrial DNA/ribosomes.

question: __________ is precipitated, when carbon dioxide is passed through lime water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaCO3 (Calcium carbonate).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lime water is a solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, in water.

 

• When carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas is passed through lime water, it reacts to form calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), an insoluble white precipitate, which turns the lime water milky: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O.

 

• This milkiness test is the standard laboratory method used to detect the presence of CO₂ gas.

 

Additional Information

 

• If excess CO₂ is passed through the milky solution for a prolonged time, the insoluble CaCO₃ converts into soluble calcium bicarbonate, Ca(HCO₃)₂, and the milkiness disappears: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂.

 

• This is also the chemistry behind the natural formation of stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves.

 

NOTE

 

• Ca(HCO3)2 (Option B): Formed only when excess CO₂ is passed, redissolving the precipitate — not the initial precipitate formed.

 

• CaSO4 (Option C): Calcium sulphate, unrelated to this reaction.

 

• Ca(OH)2 (Option D): This is lime water itself, the reactant, not the product formed.

question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 5 seconds. What is the final velocity of the car?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 m/s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Using the first equation of motion: v = u + at, where u is initial velocity, a is acceleration, and t is time.

 

• Since the car starts from rest, u = 0. Given a = 2 m/s² and t = 5 s:

 

• v = 0 + (2 × 5) = 10 m/s.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three equations of motion for uniformly accelerated bodies are: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as.

 

• These equations, formulated based on Newton's laws of motion, apply only when acceleration is constant (uniform).

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is forgetting that 'starts from rest' means u = 0 — always identify the initial velocity carefully before applying the formula.

question: Which of the following has the highest acidity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lemon juice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acidity is measured on the pH scale, where a lower pH value indicates a stronger/higher acidity (values range from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral).

 

• Lemon juice has a pH of approximately 2 to 2.5, due to the presence of citric acid, making it the most acidic among the given options.

 

• The approximate pH order here is: Lemon juice (~2.2) < Vinegar (~2.5–3) < Milk (~6.5–6.8) < Water (7, neutral), so lemon juice has the lowest pH and hence the highest acidity.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vinegar contains acetic acid and typically has a pH around 2.5–3.

 

• Milk is very mildly acidic (pH ~6.5–6.8) due to lactic acid, especially as it sours.

 

• Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7.

 

NOTE

 

• Water (Option A): Neutral, pH 7 — not acidic.

 

• Vinegar (Option B): Acidic but less so than lemon juice.

 

• Milk (Option D): Only mildly acidic, much weaker than lemon juice or vinegar.

question: The distance between the pole and the centre of curvature of a convex mirror is + 40 cm. What will be the distance between the pole and the focus of this mirror?
solution_text:
The correct answer is + 20 cm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The relationship between the radius of curvature (R) and the focal length (f) of a spherical mirror is: f = R/2.

 

• Given R = +40 cm (positive, as it's a convex mirror where distances behind the mirror are taken as positive by convention), f = 40/2 = +20 cm.

 

• For a convex mirror, both the centre of curvature and the focus lie behind the mirror (virtual side), so both R and f are taken as positive in the Cartesian sign convention.

 

Additional Information

 

• For a concave mirror, the centre of curvature and focus lie in front of the mirror, so R and f are taken as negative.

 

• Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect and diminished images, which is why they're used as rear-view/side mirrors in vehicles — they provide a wider field of view.

 

NOTE

 

• +40 cm (Option A): This is the value of R itself, not f.

 

• −20 cm and −40 cm (Options B, C): These negative values would apply to a concave mirror, not a convex mirror.

question: 11 men can dig a well 59 feet deep in 19 days. How many men can dig a well 118 feet deep in 2 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 209.

 

GIVEN

 

• 11 men dig a well 59 feet deep in 19 days.

 

• Find the number of men needed to dig a well 118 feet deep in 2 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Using the relation: (Men₁ × Days₁)/Work₁ = (Men₂ × Days₂)/Work₂, where work is the depth dug.

 

• (11 × 19)/59 = (M₂ × 2)/118.

 

• M₂ = (11 × 19 × 118)/(59 × 2).

 

• Since 118/59 = 2, this simplifies to M₂ = 11 × 19 × 2/2 = 11 × 19 = 209.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice 118 feet is exactly double of 59 feet, and the time is cut from 19 days to 2 days. So men needed = 11 × (118/59) × (19/2) = 11 × 2 × 9.5 = 209.

 

NOTE

 

• Men required is directly proportional to the work (depth) and inversely proportional to the number of days available.

question: The ratio of the volume of a sphere to the total surface area of a hemisphere is 28 : 3. If the radii of the sphere and the hemisphere are equal, find the volume of the sphere (in cubic centimetres). (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 38,808.

 

GIVEN

 

• Volume of sphere : Total surface area of hemisphere = 28 : 3 (both have the same radius r).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³. Total surface area of hemisphere = 3πr² (curved surface 2πr² + base πr²).

 

• Ratio = [(4/3)πr³] / [3πr²] = (4/9)r = 28/3.

 

• r = (28/3) × (9/4) = 21 cm.

 

• Volume of sphere = (4/3) × (22/7) × 21³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 9261.

 

• 9261/7 = 1323, so Volume = (4/3) × 22 × 1323 = (88 × 1323)/3 = 88 × 441 = 38,808 cm³.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Simplify the ratio first to isolate r directly: (4/9)r = 28/3 ⇒ r = 21. Then plug into (4/3)πr³ carefully by cancelling 21³ with the 3 and 7 in π and 4/3 to avoid large multiplications.

 

NOTE

 

• Total surface area of a hemisphere = 3πr² (this includes the flat circular base); curved surface area alone is 2πr² — a frequent point of confusion.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 2/60?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 150%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find what percentage 1/20 is of 2/60.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 2/60 simplifies to 1/30.

 

• Required % = (1/20) ÷ (1/30) × 100 = (1/20) × 30 × 100/100... more directly: (1/20)/(1/30) = 30/20 = 1.5.

 

• 1.5 = 150%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert both fractions to a common form: 1/20 = 3/60. So required % = (3/60)/(2/60) × 100 = 3/2 × 100 = 150%.

 

NOTE

 

• 'A is what % of B' always means (A/B) × 100 — keep the order of numerator/denominator correct.

question: If the third proportional of 32 and 24 is x, then what is the value of x?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 18.

 

GIVEN

 

• Third proportional of 32 and 24 is x.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For numbers a, b, the third proportional x satisfies a : b = b : x, i.e. b² = a × x.

 

• 24² = 32 × x ⇒ 576 = 32x ⇒ x = 576/32 = 18.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• x = b²/a = 24²/32 = 576/32 = 18. Memorise this direct formula to skip writing the full proportion.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse third proportional (b²/a) with mean proportional (√(ab)) — they are different concepts.

question: After selling an article at a discount of 29%, the profit percentage obtained is 4%. What is the mark-up percentage (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 46.48%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount = 29%, Profit = 4% (on cost price).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Cost Price (CP) = 100. Since profit = 4%, Selling Price (SP) = 104.

 

• Since discount = 29% on Marked Price (MP), SP = 0.71 × MP ⇒ 104 = 0.71 × MP.

 

• MP = 104/0.71 = 146.4789 (approx).

 

• Mark-up % = MP − CP = 146.4789 − 100 = 46.48% (rounded to 2 decimal places).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark-up% formula: Mark-up% = [(100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%) − 1] × 100 = [(104/71) − 1] × 100 = (33/71) × 100 ≈ 46.48%.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options in this question show an OCR artifact where the option's own leading digits were replaced by its letter (e.g. 'B).48%' actually reads 46.48%) — the computed true value 46.48% confirms Option B is correct as marked in the source.

 

• Always distinguish mark-up % (based on Cost Price) from discount % (based on Marked Price) — they use different bases.

question: If an item marked at ₹485 is sold for ₹293, then what is the discount percentage? (Round off your answer to two decimal places).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 39.59%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹485, Selling Price (SP) = ₹293.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Discount = MP − SP = 485 − 293 = ₹192.

 

• Discount % = (Discount/MP) × 100 = (192/485) × 100 = 39.5876...% ≈ 39.59%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Estimate quickly: 192/485 is close to 2/5 = 40%; precise division gives 39.59%, close to the estimate, confirming the answer.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options show an OCR artifact where the leading digits were replaced by the option's own letter (e.g. 'C).59%' actually reads 39.59%) — the computed value 39.59% confirms Option C is correctly marked.

 

• Discount % is always calculated on the Marked Price, never on the Selling Price.

question: What is the average of the first 50 even natural numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 51.

 

GIVEN

 

• First 50 even natural numbers: 2, 4, 6, ..., 100.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of first n even numbers = n(n+1). Here n = 50, so Sum = 50 × 51 = 2550.

 

• Average = Sum/n = 2550/50 = 51.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Average of the first n even natural numbers is always (n + 1). For n = 50, average = 51 directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Compare: average of first n odd natural numbers is simply n; average of first n even natural numbers is (n+1) — a useful pair of formulas to memorise.

question: The average age of four children I, J, K and L is 9 years and the average age of I, J, L, M is 12 years. K is 5 years old. The age of M (in years) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 17.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of I, J, K, L = 9 years ⇒ Sum(I+J+K+L) = 36.

 

• Average age of I, J, L, M = 12 years ⇒ Sum(I+J+L+M) = 48.

 

• K = 5 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum(I+J+L) = 36 − K = 36 − 5 = 31.

 

• M = Sum(I+J+L+M) − Sum(I+J+L) = 48 − 31 = 17.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• M − K = Sum(I+J+L+M) − Sum(I+J+K+L) = 48 − 36 = 12 ⇒ M = K + 12 = 5 + 12 = 17. This avoids computing I+J+L separately.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever two averages share three common members, subtracting the total sums directly gives the difference between the two unique members (here M and K).

question: The cost of a washing machine is 40% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 80% and that of the TV decreases by 22%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 7 washing machines and 6 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Increase by 20%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost is 40% less than TV cost. WM price rises 80%, TV price falls 22%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = 100, so WM cost = 60 (40% less than 100).

 

• Original total (7 WM + 6 TV) = 7(60) + 6(100) = 420 + 600 = 1020.

 

• New WM cost = 60 × 1.80 = 108. New TV cost = 100 × 0.78 = 78.

 

• New total = 7(108) + 6(78) = 756 + 468 = 1224.

 

• % change = [(1224 − 1020)/1020] × 100 = (204/1020) × 100 = 20% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always assume the TV's cost as 100 (a round base) so the WM's cost (40% less) comes out to a clean 60 — this keeps all further multiplication simple.

 

NOTE

 

• When two related quantities each change by different percentages, always compute total old and new values separately rather than trying to average the percentage changes directly.

question: If x² + 1 = 2x, then (x⁴ − 1) is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 0.

 

GIVEN

 

• x² + 1 = 2x.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Rearranging: x² − 2x + 1 = 0 ⇒ (x − 1)² = 0 ⇒ x = 1.

 

• x⁴ − 1 = 1⁴ − 1 = 1 − 1 = 0.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise x² + 1 = 2x as a perfect square trinomial instantly: x² − 2x + 1 = (x−1)² = 0, giving x = 1 without needing the quadratic formula.

 

NOTE

 

• Once x = 1 is found, any polynomial expression in x can be evaluated directly by substitution — no need to factor x⁴ − 1 = (x²−1)(x²+1) separately.

question: The average age of 51 students in a class is 24 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 25 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 76.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 51 students = 24 years. Including the teacher (52 people), average becomes 25 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ages of 51 students = 51 × 24 = 1224.

 

• Sum of ages of 52 people (students + teacher) = 52 × 25 = 1300.

 

• Teacher's age = 1300 − 1224 = 76 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = Old average + (New average − Old average) × New total count = 24 + (25−24) × 52 = 24 + 52 = 76.

 

NOTE

 

• This is a standard 'new entrant changes the average' problem — the extra contribution needed equals (new average) added to (increase × new count).

question: Simplify: 4 ÷ 24 + 3.6 × (1/9) − {(1/15) + (1 − 1.5)}
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• 4 ÷ 24 + 3.6 × (1/9) − {(1/15) + (1 − 1.5)}

 

SOLUTION (BODMAS: innermost brackets first)

 

• 4 ÷ 24 = 1/6 ≈ 0.1667.

 

• 3.6 × (1/9) = 0.4.

 

• Inside braces: (1 − 1.5) = −0.5, so {1/15 + (−0.5)} = 0.0667 − 0.5 = −0.4333.

 

• Full expression = 0.1667 + 0.4 − (−0.4333) = 0.5667 + 0.4333 = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert everything to fractions with a common approach: 1/6 + 2/5 − 1/15 + 1/2. LCM of 6,5,15,2 = 30: 5/30 + 12/30 − 2/30 + 15/30 = 30/30 = 1.

 

NOTE

 

• Handle the innermost brackets/braces first, and be extra careful with the sign of subtracted grouped terms — a very common place to make an error.

question: A train P going at the speed of 84 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 447 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 54 km/hr, in 4.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to completely cross train R of length 287 m, going at 87 km/hr in the opposite direction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 44.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train P (speed 84 km/hr) crosses Train Q (length 447 m, speed 54 km/hr, same direction) in 4.5 minutes.

 

• Find time for P to cross Train R (length 287 m, speed 87 km/hr, opposite direction).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Relative speed of P w.r.t. Q (same direction) = 84 − 54 = 30 km/hr = 30 × 5/18 = 25/3 m/s.

 

• Time = 4.5 min = 270 s. Distance covered while crossing = (Length of P + Length of Q) = relative speed × time = (25/3) × 270 = 2250 m.

 

• So Length of P = 2250 − 447 = 1803 m.

 

• Now, crossing R (opposite direction): relative speed = 84 + 87 = 171 km/hr = 171 × 5/18 = 47.5 m/s.

 

• Total distance to cross = Length of P + Length of R = 1803 + 287 = 2090 m.

 

• Time = 2090/47.5 = 44 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First extract the unknown length of P using the Q-crossing data (relative speed × time − known length), then directly apply it to the R-crossing scenario with the new (opposite-direction, added) relative speed.

 

NOTE

 

• Same direction ⇒ relative speed = difference of speeds; opposite direction ⇒ relative speed = sum of speeds. 'Completely crosses' always means covering the sum of both lengths.

question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 8 and 24 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 6.

 

GIVEN

 

• A, B, C alone take 3, 8, 24 days respectively for one work. Find time together for thrice the work.

 

SOLUTION

 

• One-day work of A, B, C together = 1/3 + 1/8 + 1/24.

 

• LCM of 3,8,24 = 24: = 8/24 + 3/24 + 1/24 = 12/24 = 1/2 (of the work per day).

 

• Time to complete 1 work together = 2 days.

 

• Time to complete thrice the work = 3 × 2 = 6 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take total work (LCM) = 24 units. A's rate = 8/day, B's rate = 3/day, C's rate = 1/day; combined = 12 units/day. For thrice work (3 × 24 = 72 units): time = 72/12 = 6 days.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the combined one-day work rate first by adding individual rates (1/time), then simply scale the total work required.

question: The amount on a sum of ₹6,500 at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹9,360.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal = ₹6,500, Rate = 20% p.a., Time = 2 years, compounded annually.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ = 6500 × (1.2)² = 6500 × 1.44 = ₹9,360.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 2 years, use the direct CI formula: Effective rate = R + R + (R²/100) = 20 + 20 + (400/100) = 44%. Amount = 6500 × 1.44 = ₹9,360.

 

NOTE

 

• For 2 years at rate R%, the effective growth is (2R + R²/100)% — memorising this speeds up such 2-year CI calculations considerably.

question: 3 men can do a piece of work in 20 days. How many men will do it in 2 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 30.

 

GIVEN

 

• 3 men complete a work in 20 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Using M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ (total man-days is constant for the same work): 3 × 20 = M₂ × 2.

 

• M₂ = 60/2 = 30 men.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Days reduced from 20 to 2, i.e. by a factor of 10, so men must increase by the same factor: 3 × 10 = 30.

 

NOTE

 

• Men and Days are inversely proportional when the total work is fixed — more men means fewer days needed, and vice versa.

question: A person saves 60% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹440, then his income (in ₹) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1,100.

 

GIVEN

 

• Savings = 60% of income, so expenditure = 40% of income = ₹440.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let income = I. 40% of I = 440 ⇒ I = 440 × 100/40 = ₹1,100.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expenditure (40%) : Income (100%) = 440 : I ⇒ I = 440 × (100/40) = 440 × 2.5 = ₹1,100.

 

NOTE

 

• Savings % + Expenditure % = 100% of income — always find the expenditure's percentage share first before setting up the ratio.

question: Anmol and Ayushi together invested ₹46,600 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹7,500, Anmol's share was ₹2,700. What was Anmol's investment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹16,776.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment = ₹46,600. Total profit = ₹7,500, of which Anmol's share = ₹2,700.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since the profit-sharing ratio equals the investment ratio (same time period assumed): Anmol's investment/Total investment = Anmol's profit/Total profit.

 

• Anmol's investment = 46,600 × (2,700/7,500) = 46,600 × 0.36 = ₹16,776.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 2700/7500 simplifies to 9/25 = 0.36. Multiply directly: 46,600 × 0.36 = 16,776.

 

NOTE

 

• In a partnership with the same investment duration for all partners, the profit-sharing ratio is simply the ratio of their capital invested.

question: A purse contains only ₹5 and ₹10 coins. The total number of coins is 118 and their total value is ₹855. How many coins of ₹5 are there?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 65.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total coins (₹5 + ₹10) = 118. Total value = ₹855.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let ₹5 coins = x, ₹10 coins = y. x + y = 118 ... (i); 5x + 10y = 855 ⇒ x + 2y = 171 ... (ii).

 

• Subtracting (i) from (ii): (x + 2y) − (x + y) = 171 − 118 ⇒ y = 53.

 

• x = 118 − 53 = 65.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If all 118 coins were ₹5 coins, total value would be 118 × 5 = 590. Actual excess = 855 − 590 = 265, and each ₹10 coin adds an extra ₹5 over a ₹5 coin, so ₹10 coins = 265/5 = 53, and ₹5 coins = 118 − 53 = 65.

 

NOTE

 

• This 'assume all one type, find the shortfall/excess' method is a fast alternative to solving simultaneous equations for such coin/age-mixture problems.

question: A triangular field has sides measuring 42 cm, 34 cm and 20 cm. What is the length of the altitude corresponding to the longest side?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 16 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle with sides 42 cm, 34 cm, 20 cm. Find the altitude to the longest side (42 cm).

 

SOLUTION (Heron's Formula)

 

• Semi-perimeter s = (42 + 34 + 20)/2 = 96/2 = 48.

 

• Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[48 × (48−42) × (48−34) × (48−20)] = √[48 × 6 × 14 × 28].

 

• 48 × 6 = 288; 14 × 28 = 392; 288 × 392 = 112,896. √112,896 = 336 cm².

 

• Altitude to the longest side (42 cm) = 2 × Area/Base = (2 × 336)/42 = 672/42 = 16 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Area = ½ × base × height, so height = 2 × Area/base — once Heron's formula gives the area, dividing is the fastest route to the altitude.

 

NOTE

 

• The altitude corresponding to the longest side is always the shortest of the three possible altitudes of a triangle (since Area = ½ × base × height is constant, a larger base means a smaller height).

question: Mohan buys a watch for ₹460 and sells it for ₹483. Find his percentage of profit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 5%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost Price (CP) = ₹460, Selling Price (SP) = ₹483.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Profit = SP − CP = 483 − 460 = ₹23.

 

• Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (23/460) × 100 = 5%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 23 is exactly 1/20th of 460, and 1/20 = 5%, so the profit percentage is directly 5% without long division.

 

NOTE

 

• Profit/Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price, never on the Selling Price, unless a question explicitly states otherwise.

question: In a ΔPMN, ∠P = 76°. The bisectors of the exterior angles at M and N intersect each other at point O. The degree measure of ∠MON is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 52°.

 

GIVEN

 

• In ΔPMN, ∠P = 76°. Bisectors of exterior angles at M and N meet at O.

 

SOLUTION

 

• There is a standard result: if the bisectors of the exterior angles at two vertices (M, N) of a triangle meet at O, then ∠MON = 90° − (∠P)/2.

 

• ∠MON = 90° − 76°/2 = 90° − 38° = 52°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember the three standard 'bisector meeting point' formulas for a triangle with vertex angle A: internal-internal bisectors meet at 90° + A/2; external-external bisectors (as here) meet at 90° − A/2; one internal, one external bisector meet at A/2.

 

NOTE

 

• Here, since the exterior angle bisectors of M and N are used (not internal bisectors), the applicable formula is 90° − A/2, not 90° + A/2 — a common point of confusion.

question: If cos θ = 5/13, then find the value of √[(1 − sin θ)/(1 + sin θ)].
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1/5.

 

GIVEN

 

• cos θ = 5/13.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Using a 5-12-13 Pythagorean triplet (right triangle with base 5, height 12, hypotenuse 13): sin θ = 12/13.

 

• (1 − sin θ)/(1 + sin θ) = (1 − 12/13)/(1 + 12/13) = (1/13)/(25/13) = 1/25.

 

• √(1/25) = 1/5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise that √[(1−sinθ)/(1+sinθ)] simplifies algebraically to (secθ − tanθ). With cosθ = 5/13, sinθ = 12/13: secθ − tanθ = 13/5 − 12/5 = 1/5. Same answer, faster route.

 

NOTE

 

• Always identify the standard Pythagorean triplet (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, etc.) hidden in the given ratio — it instantly gives the other trigonometric ratios without needing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 explicitly.

question: Simplify: [72 ÷ {6 × (3 + 2)} + 5² − 8] × 5 / 97
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• [72 ÷ {6 × (3 + 2)} + 5² − 8] × 5 / 97

 

SOLUTION (BODMAS)

 

• Innermost bracket: (3 + 2) = 5. Then {6 × 5} = 30.

 

• 72 ÷ 30 = 2.4.

 

• 5² = 25.

 

• Inside the square brackets: 2.4 + 25 − 8 = 19.4.

 

• 19.4 × 5 = 97. Then 97/97 = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice the final division is by 97 — once you compute the bracket value (19.4) and multiply by 5 to get exactly 97, the answer must simplify to 1. This is a strong hint the numbers were designed to cancel neatly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always resolve nested brackets from the innermost pair outward, following BODMAS strictly: Bracket → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

question: Two trains, measuring 267 metres and 153 metres in length, are moving in the same direction at speeds of 162 km/hr and 36 km/hr, respectively. How long will it take for the faster train to completely overtake the slower one?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 12 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train lengths: 267 m and 153 m. Speeds: 162 km/hr and 36 km/hr, same direction.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Relative speed (same direction) = 162 − 36 = 126 km/hr = 126 × 5/18 = 35 m/s.

 

• To completely overtake, the faster train must cover the sum of both lengths: 267 + 153 = 420 m.

 

• Time = Distance/Speed = 420/35 = 12 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert speed to m/s using the shortcut ×5/18: 126 × 5/18 = 7 × 5 = 35 m/s (cancel 126/18 = 7 first). Then 420/35 = 12 s directly.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Completely overtake/cross' problems always require covering the sum of the lengths of both trains, using the relative speed appropriate to their direction of motion.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

 

(Left) 5 7 1 8 4 2 3 9 5 7 6 1 (Right)

 

How many even numbers are there which are immediately followed by odd numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 5, 7, 1, 8, 4, 2, 3, 9, 5, 7, 6, 1.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check each even number and see if the number immediately after it is odd:

 

• 8 (pos 4) → next is 4 (even) — No.

 

• 4 (pos 5) → next is 2 (even) — No.

 

• 2 (pos 6) → next is 3 (odd) — Yes (1).

 

• 6 (pos 11) → next is 1 (odd) — Yes (2).

 

• Total count = Two.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Scan only the even numbers in the sequence and check just their very next neighbour — no need to examine odd numbers at all, since the condition only cares about what follows an even number.

 

NOTE

 

• Always work strictly left to right as instructed, and be careful with the last element of the series — it has no 'next' number to check.

question: EFJL is related to HKMQ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, QZVF is related to TEYK. To which of the following options is ZOEU related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. CTHZ.

 

GIVEN

 

• EFJL → HKMQ, and QZVF → TEYK follow the same logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check letter-by-letter shifts for EFJL→HKMQ: E(+3)=H, F(+5)=K, J(+3)=M, L(+5)=Q. Pattern: +3, +5, +3, +5.

 

• Verify with QZVF→TEYK: Q(+3)=T, Z(+5, wraps)=E (Z=26, 26+5=31, 31−26=5=E), V(+3)=Y, F(+5)=K. Pattern confirmed: +3, +5, +3, +5.

 

• Apply to ZOEU: Z(+3, wraps)=C (26+3=29, 29−26=3=C), O(+5)=T, E(+3)=H, U(+5)=Z.

 

• Result: CTHZ.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to their alphabet positions (A=1...Z=26), find the alternating shift pattern from the FIRST given pair, confirm it with the SECOND given pair, then apply directly — remember to wrap around past Z back to A.

 

NOTE

 

• This is a classic alternating-shift coding pattern (+3, +5, +3, +5); always verify your discovered pattern against BOTH given example pairs before applying it to the new word.

question: Mukesh starts from Point A and drives 14 km towards the North. He then takes a left turn, drives 9 km, then turns left and drives 17 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 13 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 3 km, and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 4 km to the west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Legs: 14 km North → Left turn, 9 km → Left turn, 17 km → Left turn, 13 km → Left turn, 3 km, ending at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A as origin (0,0), facing North initially. Track direction after each left turn: North → West → South → East → North.

 

• Leg 1: North 14 km → (0, 14).

 

• Leg 2 (West) 9 km → (−9, 14).

 

• Leg 3 (South) 17 km → (−9, −3).

 

• Leg 4 (East) 13 km → (4, −3).

 

• Leg 5 (North) 3 km → (4, 0).

 

• Final position P = (4, 0), i.e. 4 km east of A. So to return to A, Mukesh must drive 4 km to the west.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Plot the path on a simple x-y grid, treating North/South as the y-axis and East/West as the x-axis; add up all North/South movements for the y-coordinate and all East/West movements for the x-coordinate separately, then find the final point directly.

 

NOTE

 

• With four consecutive left turns starting from North, the direction cycles N→W→S→E→N — track this cycle carefully leg by leg to avoid direction errors.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. C sits third to the right of D. E sits second to the right of C. F is the immediate neighbour of both B and C. G is not an immediate neighbour of D. How many people sit between A and G when counted from the left of G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people, circular table, facing centre. Conditions on C, E, F, G relative to D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Place D at position 0. C is third to the right of D ⇒ C = position 3. E is second to the right of C ⇒ E = position 5.

 

• Remaining seats {1, 2, 4, 6} are for A, B, F, G.

 

• F must be an immediate neighbour of C (position 3), so F is at position 2 or 4.

 

• G is NOT an immediate neighbour of D (positions 1 and 6 are D's neighbours), so G must be at position 2 or 4 too.

 

• F is also a neighbour of B. Testing F=2 (neighbours are 1 and 3): B must be at 1 (since 3 is C). This leaves G=4, and A=6 (the only seat left).

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise from D=0): D(0), B(1), F(2), C(3), G(4), E(5), A(6).

 

• Counting from the left (counter-clockwise) of G(4): 4→3(C)→2(F)→1(B)→0(D)→6(A). The people between G and A on this path are C, F, B, D = 4 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix one person (D) at a reference position, translate every 'right of X' clue into a seat number using clockwise = right, and resolve ambiguous seats (like F's two options) using the secondary neighbour condition to eliminate the invalid case.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Counted from the left of G' means you must travel counter-clockwise starting at G — always fix a direction convention (clockwise = right) at the start and apply it consistently throughout.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 11 × 22 + 288 ÷ 18 − 50 = ?

• 242 + 16 − 50 = 258 − 50 = 208.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. CIE.

 

GIVEN

 

• Clusters: IOL, GMJ, CIE, PVS.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the pattern of gaps between the 1st-2nd and 2nd-3rd letters in each cluster:

 

• IOL: I(9)→O(15) = +6; O(15)→L(12) = −3.

 

• GMJ: G(7)→M(13) = +6; M(13)→J(10) = −3.

 

• PVS: P(16)→V(22) = +6; V(22)→S(19) = −3.

 

• CIE: C(3)→I(9) = +6; I(9)→E(5) = −4 (breaks the pattern).

 

• IOL, GMJ and PVS all follow the (+6, −3) pattern, but CIE follows (+6, −4) — it is the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each letter to its alphabet position and compute the gap between consecutive letters in each cluster; group clusters sharing the identical gap-pattern and spot the mismatch.

 

NOTE

 

• Since three clusters share an identical two-step gap pattern, the fourth one — even if it looks visually similar — must be the exception.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

(3, -2, 11)

(46, 2107, 9)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. (34, 1135, 21).

 

GIVEN

 

• (3, −2, 11) and (46, 2107, 9) follow a common logic; find the option that follows the same logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test the relation: (1st number)² − (2nd number) = 3rd number.

 

• Set 1: 3² − (−2) = 9 + 2 = 11 ✓ (matches given 3rd number).

 

• Set 2: 46² − 2107 = 2116 − 2107 = 9 ✓ (matches given 3rd number).

 

• Pattern confirmed: a² − b = c.

 

• Check Option B (34, 1135, 21): 34² − 1135 = 1156 − 1135 = 21 ✓ — matches exactly.

 

• Quickly verifying the others fails: (A) 33²−1081=1089−1081=8≠7; (C) 25²−607=625−607=18≠17; (D) 38²−1433=1444−1433=11≠10.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With three numbers given, always test the simplest possible relations first — sum, difference, product, or one number squared minus another — starting with the two smaller/more manageable numbers to find 'a² − b = c' quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the note disallows digit-breaking, focus purely on whole-number arithmetic operations (squares, sums, differences, products) between the numbers as given.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

Some oranges are peaches.

No peach is a carrot.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some oranges are carrots.

(II) All carrots are peaches.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Some oranges are peaches (I-type statement).

 

• No peach is a carrot (E-type statement).

 

SOLUTION

 

• From 'Some oranges are peaches' and 'No peach is a carrot', by the standard syllogism rule for an I + E combination, the valid conclusion possible is 'Some oranges are not carrots' — not 'Some oranges are carrots'.

 

• Conclusion I ('Some oranges are carrots') directly contradicts what can be validly derived, so it does not follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('All carrots are peaches') is an unsupported universal claim — the statements only tell us peaches and carrots have NO overlap; nothing suggests all carrots are peaches. It does not follow.

 

• Hence, neither conclusion follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use Venn diagrams: draw overlapping circles for oranges-peaches (partial overlap) and completely separate circles for peaches-carrots (no overlap) — visually check whether oranges and carrots circles are forced to overlap (they are not, since carrots' relation to oranges is undefined).

 

NOTE

 

• A particular affirmative (I) premise combined with a universal negative (E) premise, sharing a common middle term, yields only a particular negative conclusion about the two end terms — never a positive one like Conclusion I here.

question:

question: SDFH is related to VYIC in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, EJRN is related to HEUI. To which of the following options is NUAY related, following the same logic?

SOLUTION

 

• Check shifts for SDFH→VYIC: S(+3)=V, D(−5, i.e. wraps: 4−5=−1→+26=25)=Y, F(+3)=I, H(−5, wraps: 8−5=3)=C. Pattern: +3, −5, +3, −5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

• When a shift goes below 'A' (position 1), add 26 to wrap around to the end of the alphabet, just like adding 26 when going past 'Z'.

question: Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K and L are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only I is kept above C. Only L is kept between C and J. Only K is kept below D. How many boxes are kept between B and I?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked vertically. Conditions relate I, C, L, J, K, D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only I is kept above C' ⇒ I is the topmost box, and C is directly below it (position 6 from bottom, out of 7).

 

• 'Only L is kept between C and J' ⇒ exactly one box (L) lies between C and J. Since nothing can be above C except I, J must be below C, giving order (top to bottom): I, C, L, J.

 

• 'Only K is kept below D' ⇒ D is second from the bottom, and K is the bottommost box.

 

• The one remaining box, B, takes the only leftover position, just below J and above D.

 

• Full stack (top to bottom): I, C, L, J, B, D, K.

 

• Boxes between B and I: positions occupied by J, L, C — that's 3 boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the two 'only ___ is above/below' clues first (they pin down the very top and very bottom boxes directly), then slot in the 'between' clue as a fixed three-box block, leaving only one position for the remaining box.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only X is above/below Y' is the strongest type of clue in stacking puzzles — it fixes an exact position (topmost or bottommost) immediately.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

NOTE

 

• Always verify an alternating multiplication pattern across all given terms (not just the first pair) before extending it, since coincidental matches with just two terms are possible.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. From the given options, select the one which follows the same logic.

MIST - TIMS - ISMT

HOPE - EOHP - OPHE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. BUSY - YUBS - USBY.

 

GIVEN

 

• MIST → TIMS → ISMT, and HOPE → EOHP → OPHE follow the same logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the position-mapping from word 1 to word 2 for MIST(1:M,2:I,3:S,4:T)→TIMS: new1=old4(T), new2=old2(I), new3=old1(M), new4=old3(S) → mapping [4,2,1,3].

 

• Verify with HOPE(1:H,2:O,3:P,4:E)→EOHP: new1=old4(E), new2=old2(O), new3=old1(H), new4=old3(P) → same mapping [4,2,1,3] ✓.

 

• Find the mapping from word 2 to word 3, using TIMS(1:T,2:I,3:M,4:S)→ISMT: new1=old2(I), new2=old4(S), new3=old3(M), new4=old1(T) → mapping [2,4,3,1].

 

• Verify with EOHP(1:E,2:O,3:H,4:P)→OPHE: new1=old2(O), new2=old4(P), new3=old3(H), new4=old1(E) → same mapping [2,4,3,1] ✓.

 

• Apply mapping [4,2,1,3] to BUSY(1:B,2:U,3:S,4:Y): new1=old4(Y), new2=old2(U), new3=old1(B), new4=old3(S) → YUBS ✓ (matches given).

 

• Apply mapping [2,4,3,1] to YUBS(1:Y,2:U,3:B,4:S): new1=old2(U), new2=old4(S), new3=old3(B), new4=old1(Y) → USBY ✓ (matches given).

 

• Both transformations match Option B exactly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Number the letters of the first word 1-2-3-4, work out exactly which original position each letter of the second word came from, and that same positional 'recipe' must reproduce the third word from the second — test this recipe against the answer options rather than guessing.

 

NOTE

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

834 840 848 ? 870 884
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 858.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 834, 840, 848, ?, 870, 884.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences: 840−834=6, 848−840=8, 870−884(unknown yet)..., 884−870=14.

 

• The differences follow the pattern: 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (each increasing by 2).

 

• Missing difference (3rd gap) = 10, so ? = 848 + 10 = 858.

 

• Verify: next gap = 12 ⇒ 858 + 12 = 870 ✓; next gap = 14 ⇒ 870 + 14 = 884 ✓.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the LAST two known differences (12 between 870→858 backward, and 14 between 884→870) to work backward and confirm the pattern, which is often faster than working purely forward when the missing term is in the middle.

 

NOTE

 

• This is a second-order series where the differences themselves increase steadily (by 2 each time) — always check both ends of the sequence to pin down the pattern precisely.

question:
If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

43 − 17 ÷ 147 + 362 × 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 697.

 

GIVEN

 

• 43 − 17 ÷ 147 + 362 × 2 = ?, where + means −, − means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute each symbol with its real meaning: '−' → ×, '÷' → +, '+' → −, '×' → ÷.

 

• Expression becomes: 43 × 17 + 147 − 362 ÷ 2 = ?

 

• Applying BODMAS: Division first: 362 ÷ 2 = 181. Multiplication: 43 × 17 = 731.

 

• 731 + 147 − 181 = 878 − 181 = 697.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the entire expression with the TRUE operators substituted for ALL four symbols in one pass before doing any arithmetic — mixing substitution and calculation together is where most errors creep in.

 

NOTE

 

• Even after substitution, standard BODMAS order still applies to the new (real) operators — division and multiplication are still done before addition and subtraction.

question: Seven people, B, C, D, I, J, K and L, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. I sits to the immediate left of D. J is the immediate neighbour of both B and K. K sits third to the left of D. L is not an immediate neighbour of K. Who sits second to the right of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. D.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people around a circular table facing the centre; conditions on I, J, K, L relative to D and each other.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix D at position 0 (clockwise = right, counter-clockwise = left).

 

• I is immediate left of D ⇒ I = position 6 (one step counter-clockwise).

 

• K is third to the left of D ⇒ K = position 4 (three steps counter-clockwise).

 

• J is an immediate neighbour of K(4), so J = position 3 or 5. J is also a neighbour of B.

 

• Testing J=3: neighbours of J are position 2 and 4(K), so B must be at position 2.

 

• Remaining positions {1, 5} go to C and L. Since L cannot be an immediate neighbour of K (positions 3 and 5), L cannot be at 5, so L = 1, C = 5.

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise from D=0): D(0), L(1), B(2), J(3), K(4), C(5), I(6).

 

• Second to the right (clockwise) of C(5): 5+2 = 7 mod 7 = 0 = D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the vertex with the most direct clues (D here) at position 0, resolve each 'left/right of D' clue into a definite seat number, and use the neighbour clues to disambiguate between the remaining candidate seats.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Third to the left' means three steps counter-clockwise, landing on the fourth position along that path (not the third) — a common off-by-one trap.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the sister of B',

A @ B means 'A is the brother of B',

A − B means 'A is the wife of B' and

A # B means 'A is the father of B'.

Based on the above, how is O related to V if 'O + P @ T − G # V'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Mother's sister.

 

GIVEN

 

• O + P → O is sister of P.

 

• P @ T → P is brother of T.

 

• T − G → T is wife of G.

 

• G # V → G is father of V.

 

SOLUTION

 

• P is the brother of T, and O is the sister of P, so O, P and T are all siblings — hence O is also the sister of T.

 

• T is the wife of G, and G is the father of V, so T is V's mother (G's wife = mother of G's children).

 

• Since O is T's sister, and T is V's mother, O is V's maternal aunt, i.e. O is V's Mother's sister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Redraw the coded chain as a simple family tree step by step (O–P, P–T, T–G, G–V), labelling each relationship as you go — this prevents losing track of generations in multi-step blood-relation puzzles.

 

NOTE

 

• Since P is BOTH sister of O and brother of T, all three (O, P, T) belong to the same sibling generation — a key deduction that unlocks the rest of the chain.

question: A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. Only two people sit between C and U when counted from the left of U. B sits third to the left of A. T sits to the immediate right of A. T sits second to the left of C. R is not an immediate neighbour of B. Who sits third to the right of S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. T.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people around a circular table facing the centre; conditions relate A, B, C, T, U, R, S.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix A at position 0 (clockwise = right, counter-clockwise = left).

 

• T is immediate right of A ⇒ T = position 1.

 

• T is second to the left of C ⇒ C = T + 2 = position 3.

 

• B is third to the left of A ⇒ B = position 0 − 3 = position 4 (mod 7).

 

• Only two people sit between C and U counted from the left of U ⇒ moving counter-clockwise from U, two people are passed before reaching C, so U = C + 3 = 3 + 3 = position 6.

 

• Remaining positions {2, 5} go to R and S. R is not an immediate neighbour of B(4): neighbours of 4 are 3(C) and 5, so R ≠ 5, meaning R = 2, S = 5.

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise from A=0): A(0), T(1), R(2), C(3), B(4), S(5), U(6).

 

• Third to the right (clockwise) of S(5): 5 + 3 = 8 mod 7 = 1 = T.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain the clues starting from the person with the most 'anchor' clues (A here has two direct clues), convert every left/right statement into a fixed seat number one at a time, and resolve the last ambiguous pair using the 'not a neighbour of' condition.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Two people between C and U counted from the left of U' means U is exactly 3 seats counter-clockwise from C, i.e. C is 3 seats clockwise from U — always convert 'x people between' into '(x+1) seats apart' carefully.

question: Raman ranked 31st from the top and 12th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 42.

 

GIVEN

 

• Raman's rank = 31st from the top, 12th from the bottom.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total students = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1, since Raman himself is counted in both ranks.

 

• Total = 31 + 12 − 1 = 42.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK
