NOTE

 

• This formula (Total = Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1) applies whenever a single position is described from both ends of a line-up or ranking.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

Some paddy are rice.

Some rice are wheat.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some paddy are wheat.

(II) All wheat are rice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Some paddy are rice (I-type).

 

• Some rice are wheat (I-type).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Both statements are particular affirmative (I-type) propositions sharing the common middle term 'rice'.

 

• The standard syllogism rule states that two particular (I-type) premises never yield any valid conclusion — the middle term 'rice' is not proven to be fully distributed in either statement, so no definite link between paddy and wheat can be established.

 

• Hence, Conclusion I ('Some paddy are wheat') does NOT necessarily follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('All wheat are rice') is a universal claim not supported at all by 'Some rice are wheat' (which only guarantees partial overlap, not that all wheat is rice).

 

• Therefore, neither conclusion follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• As a quick rule of thumb: 'Some + Some' with a shared middle term never gives a valid conclusion — you can eliminate such option pairs almost instantly without drawing Venn diagrams.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful not to assume transitivity (Some A are B, Some B are C ⇒ Some A are C) — this is a very common but logically invalid shortcut in syllogism questions.

question:
Refer to the number series given below and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only.

(NOTE: All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

 

(Left) 3 1 3 9 6 3 4 1 1 5 6 9 9 6 8 9 7 5 6 6 2 (Right)

 

How many such even digits are there each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 3, 1, 3, 9, 6, 3, 4, 1, 1, 5, 6, 9, 9, 6, 8, 9, 7, 5, 6, 6, 2.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Single-digit perfect squares: 0, 1, 4, 9.

 

• Check every even digit in the series to see if it is (a) immediately preceded by a perfect square, AND (b) immediately followed by another even digit:

 

◦ 6 (after 9, before 3): preceded by perfect square (9) ✓, but followed by 3 (odd) ✗.

 

◦ 4 (after 3, before 1): preceded by 3 (not a perfect square) ✗.

 

◦ 6 (after 5, before 9): preceded by 5 (not PS) ✗.

 

◦ 6 (after 9, before 8): preceded by perfect square (9) ✓, followed by 8 (even) ✓ — MATCH!

 

◦ 8 (after 6, before 9): preceded by 6 (not PS) ✗.

 

◦ 6 (after 5, before 6): preceded by 5 (not PS) ✗.

 

◦ 6 (after 6, before 2): preceded by 6 (not PS) ✗.

 

◦ 2 (last digit, after 6): preceded by 6 (not PS), and has no following digit anyway ✗.

 

• Only one even digit (the '6' that appears between the second '9' and '8') satisfies both conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Scan the series and mark only the even digits first (ignore all odd digits entirely), then check just the immediate neighbours of each marked digit against the two conditions — this narrows the search space considerably.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember that 0, 1, 4, and 9 are the only single-digit perfect squares (0²,1²,2²,3²) — don't forget 0 and 1 are valid perfect squares too, even though none appear as neighbours here.

question: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. IL - EL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: OR-KN, IL-EL, PS-LO, MP-IL.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the letter-position difference for both letters of each pair:

 

• OR-KN: O(15)−K(11) = 4; R(18)−N(14) = 4. Pattern: (+4, +4).

 

• PS-LO: P(16)−L(12) = 4; S(19)−O(15) = 4. Pattern: (+4, +4).

 

• MP-IL: M(13)−I(9) = 4; P(16)−L(12) = 4. Pattern: (+4, +4).

 

• IL-EL: I(9)−E(5) = 4; L(12)−L(12) = 0 (breaks the pattern).

 

• OR-KN, PS-LO and MP-IL all follow the consistent (+4, +4) shift, but IL-EL follows (+4, 0) — the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert both letters of each pair to their alphabet numbers and find the difference for each letter position; group pairs sharing an identical pair of differences and spot the mismatch.

 

NOTE

 

• Even though IL-EL 'looks' similar (shares the letter L), the actual numeric shift pattern reveals it doesn't belong — always verify with numbers, not visual similarity.

question: Hemant starts from Point A and drives 3 km towards the east. He then takes a right turn, drives 5 km, turns right and drives 6 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 5 km, takes a final left turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 11 km towards the east.

 

GIVEN

 

• Legs: 3 km East → Right, 5 km → Right, 6 km → Right, 5 km → Left, 8 km, ending at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A as origin (0,0), facing East initially.

 

• Leg 1: East 3 km → (3, 0).

 

• Turn Right (from East) → South. Leg 2: South 5 km → (3, −5).

 

• Turn Right (from South) → West. Leg 3: West 6 km → (−3, −5).

 

• Turn Right (from West) → North. Leg 4: North 5 km → (−3, 0).

 

• Turn Left (from North) → West. Leg 5: West 8 km → (−11, 0).

 

• Final position P = (−11, 0), i.e. 11 km west of A. So to return to A, Hemant must drive 11 km to the east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track direction changes on a simple compass (E→S→W→N cycle for right turns, reversing to W for the final left turn), and sum up the East/West and North/South components separately to pinpoint the final position quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Notice legs 2 and 4 (both North-South, 5 km each in opposite directions) cancel out completely, leaving only the East-West components (3−6−8 = −11) to determine the final answer.
